title: Cut the Rod for the Best Price

concept.title: The first piece of the cut can have any length; the rest is a smaller rod
body: A rod has the length `n` (a whole number). A shop buys pieces of any whole length from 1 to `n`, paying a given price for each length, and the prices need not grow evenly. You may cut the rod into several pieces (or not cut at all) and sell all the pieces. What is the **largest total price**? With the prices `1 5 8 9 10 17 17 20` for the lengths 1 to 8, a rod of length 8 is best cut into 2 + 6 for 5 + 17 = 22.

Let `best(L)` be the largest price for a rod of length `L`, with `best(0) = 0`. Look at the **first piece**: its length is some `c` from 1 to `L`, it brings `price(c)`, and what remains is a rod of the length `L - c`, which can be sold as well as possible: **`best(L) = max over c from 1 to L of price(c) + best(L - c)`**. The table is filled from short rods to long ones.

body.code:
best = [0] * (n + 1)
for length in range(1, n + 1):
    top = 0
    for cut in range(1, length + 1):
        top = max(top, price[cut - 1] + best[length - cut])
    best[length] = top
print(best[n])

body: This is the unbounded knapsack again: the "items" are the piece lengths, the "capacity" is the rod, and a length can be used many times. Here every cell tries all `L` first pieces, so the time is O(n^2) (4 million steps at the limit) and the memory O(n). Always check whether a recurrence over "the first/last choice" gives a new problem of the same kind but smaller.

statement: A rod has the length `n`. For every whole length `i` from 1 to `n` a piece of that length can be sold for `price[i]`. The rod may be cut into any number of pieces of whole lengths (also not cut at all), and all the pieces are sold. Print the largest total price.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the length of the rod.
The second line has `n` numbers: `price[i]` is the price of a piece of length `i` (the lengths are 1 to `n`).
hints: Let best(L) be the largest price for a rod of length L; best(0) = 0.
The first piece has some length c: best(L) = max(price(c) + best(L - c)).
Fill the table for L = 1, 2, ..., n.

explanation: best(L) = the largest over the length c of the first piece of price(c) + best(L - c), with best(0) = 0, filled for increasing L; the answer is best(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
price = list(map(int, input().split()))

best = [0] * (n + 1)
for length in range(1, n + 1):
    top = 0
    for cut in range(1, length + 1):
        v = price[cut - 1] + best[length - cut]
        if v > top:
            top = v
    best[length] = top
print(best[n])
